title: Say hello
intro: A program is a set of instructions. Start by asking Axiom to write a message.
explanation: print(...) sends a value to the output panel. Double quotes mark text. The semicolon ends the instruction. Click Run and check to execute this program.
challenge: Run the starter program. Your output should match the target below.
hint: You do not need to change anything for the first step. Click Run and check.
takeaway: You wrote Axiom source. Its compiler checked it, produced bytecode, and the virtual machine printed your message.

title: Remember a value
intro: Give a value a name so you can use it again.
explanation: let creates a variable. score is its name, number is its type, and = gives it a starting value. Numbers have no quotes. score + 5 adds five to the value stored in score.
challenge: Change the starting score so the program prints 20.
hint: The program adds 5 before printing. Which starting value plus 5 gives 20?
takeaway: A variable has both a value and a type. Axiom checks those types before your program runs.

title: Build a message
intro: Combine words with information from your program.
explanation: A string is text inside double quotes. + joins two strings. str(score) converts the number into text first. Axiom makes that conversion explicit so adding numbers and joining text stay predictable.
challenge: Change score so the message says Score: 12.
hint: Keep the message and str(...) as they are. Change the number stored in score.
takeaway: str(value) converts numbers and booleans to text. len("Axiom") returns 5. Try both in the full studio.

title: Make a decision
intro: Choose an instruction based on whether something is true.
explanation: if checks the condition inside parentheses. >= means greater than or equal to. The first pair of braces runs when the condition is true; else runs when it is false.
challenge: Change temperature so the program prints Warm.
hint: The first branch runs for a temperature of 20 or more.
takeaway: Conditions produce a boolean: true or false. Axiom requires a boolean condition instead of guessing what a number means.

title: Repeat an instruction
intro: Let the computer do repetitive work for you.
explanation: while repeats the instructions inside its braces while the condition is true. count = count + 1 increases the counter each time. That update eventually makes the condition false and ends the loop.
challenge: Change the condition so the program prints 1, 2, 3, and 4 on separate lines.
hint: The current condition stops at 3. Keep the counter update and change the upper bound.
takeaway: A loop needs a way to finish. Axiom also has an instruction budget to stop accidental infinite loops.

title: Make your own tool
intro: Name a useful calculation and call it whenever you need it.
explanation: fn declares a function. double accepts a number named n and returns a number. return sends the result back to the caller. double(4) calls the function with 4 as its argument.
challenge: Change the call so the program prints 12.
hint: double multiplies its input by 2. Which input produces 12?
takeaway: You can now write output, variables, text, decisions, loops, and functions. Open your code in the studio to inspect how each instruction works.
